title.analysis: Authentic title "Why Everything Changes After You Hit $500,000 Invested" promises a threshold explanation. The script delivers the crossover-point idea, fee and behaviour-gap warnings, and options (Coast FIRE, geographic arbitrage, products), with a candid reality check that $500K is not rich. The "everything changes" promise rests on expected, not guaranteed, returns.

script.opening_words: Meet Alan, 32 years old, makes 70 grand a year doing something with spreadsheets that he couldn't explain to you if you asked. He's been investing for 6 years, every paycheck a chunk goes straight into his index funds. He's done everything right, and his account just crossed $48,000. He does the math one night after his third beer and realizes at this rate he'll hit a million dollars right around the time he turns 78. He considers throwing his
script.ending_words: work alone. Everything after that gets easier, faster, more automatic. $500,000 looks like a mountain until you're standing on it. Then, you look down and realize most of the climbing happened in the first third of the trip, and the rest was just not quitting. The machine just needs time. Your only job is to keep feeding it and stop trying to help. I'll see you in the next one.
script.analysis: Full 19530 canonical characters read. A single-narrator story-driven explainer with composite Alan (and George as foil): hook on Alan at $48K, crossover point at 8-10%, median-income comparison, Munger quote, milestone timeline, doubling time, 1% fee drag, concentration risk, Alan at $512K, Coast FIRE, geographic arbitrage, product access, lifestyle creep, Morningstar and Dalbar behaviour gaps, Barber and Odean, boredom gambling, reality check (4% rule, tax on traditional accounts, SCF rarity), Alan vs George at 60, close. Most headline arithmetic reproduces; the milestone timeline does not, the Alan path is internally inconsistent and future crashes are narrated as past events.
